title: Abstract 4609: Prevention of pancreatic cancer using novel crocetin compound
abstract: Abstract                Pancreatic cancer is one of the most lethal malignancies in humans and there is no effective conventional treatment available for the cure of patients with pancreatic cancer. Great demand of new effective drugs and alternative approaches has led to studies evaluating possible anti-cancer agents in fruits, vegetables, herbs and spices. Crocetin, a carotenoid molecule isolated from saffron, has been demonstrated recently by our laboratory that crocetin treatment has potent antimitotic effects on both in vitro and in vivo pancreatic cancer models. Commercial crocetin is a mixture of crocetin esters and recently, novel crocetin compound and its esters are also fractionated from commercial crocetin by us using prepartory HPLC and LC/MS.The aim of this work is to identify most potent fractions separted from crude or commecial crocetin following the signaling mechanisms, responsible for inducing cellular proliferation and tumorigenesis of pancreatic adenocarcinoma. One of the fractions separated from crude crocetin by preparative HPLC, and identified using LC/MS and NMR as crocetinic acid, markedly regressed the proliferation and increased apoptosis in pancreatic cancer cells. Growth related signaling pathways such as epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR) and its down-stream signaling molecule, Akt phosphorylation were significantly altered by novel crocetin compound derived from crude crocetin. It has also been demonstrated that novel crocetin compound altered histone deacetylase (HDAC) and its substrate acetyl histone H3 Lysine14 that indicates histone modifications by inhibition of deacetylation. Apoptosis was significantly stimulated as indicated by Bax/Bcl-2 ratio by treatment with purified crocetin. Purified crocetin compound showed significant anti-tumorigenic effect at lower doses than commercial or crude crocetin using proliferation and apoptosis as markers. Crocetin can be used as chemopreventive agent for pancreatic cancer in future.                Citation Format: {Authors}. {Abstract title} [abstract]. In: Proceedings of the 102nd Annual Meeting of the American Association for Cancer Research; 2011 Apr 2-6; Orlando, FL.
